entities.summary:
Clitomachus of Thebes (b. unknown, Thebes) was a renowned athlete in the Classical era, a period of significant cultural, philosophical, and political change in the ancient world. He was known for his remarkable athletic achievements in the Olympic Games.


Clitomachus's athletic prowess was a notable aspect of the Classical era, a time when sports and physical culture played a significant role in the development of Western civilization. His achievements in the Olympic Games helped establish Thebes as a major center of athletic excellence in ancient Greece.


The legacy of Clitomachus of Thebes can be seen in the continued importance of athletic competition in modern times, as well as the enduring impact of ancient Greek culture on Western society.


As the saying goes, 'the greatest glory in living lies not in never falling, but in rising every time we fall,' a sentiment that echoes the resilience and determination that defined Clitomachus's remarkable athletic career.
